text: Gvulot (Hebrew: גְּבוּלוֹת, lit. 'Borders') is a kibbutz in southern Israel, situated in the north-western Negev desert and under the jurisdiction of the Eshkol Regional Council. As of 2023, it had a population of 438 and is located approximately 120 meters above sea level. The village was established on land owned by the Jewish National Fund (JNF) on 12 May 1943 by immigrants from Romania and Turkey, who were members of the "Kibbutz Eretz Israel Gimel" group of Hashomer Hatzair, with financial support from Keren Hayesod. It was initially named Mitzpe Gvulot (Hebrew: מִצְפֶּה גְּבוּלוֹת, lit. 'Borders lookout') and was the first of three lookouts, the others being Beit Eshel and Revivim. Gvulot was the second modern Jewish settlement in the Negev and the first in the Gaza area, with the primary purpose of guarding JNF land and conducting research on the region's soil and climate to assess agricultural suitability. It was officially recognized as a kibbutz in 1946. Prior to the 1948 Arab–Israeli War, the settlement was divided into two parts—a small group of families in its post-war location and the rest in a nearby military base. During the war, the base served the 8th Brigade. After the war, in 1949, all residents relocated to Gvulot's current site, about 1.5 kilometers south of the base. Simon Le Bon, the lead singer of Duran Duran, worked at Kibbutz Gvulot, where he wrote early lyrics for "Careless Memories", "The Chauffeur", "Sound of Thunder", and "Tel Aviv". An anaerobic waste plant is currently being constructed between Gvulot and Tzeelim.
